lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: This is a fictional boardroom with five original animal executives and one sealed archive. The products are real; the meeting is a teaching story.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: Welcome to the board. Oh, good, you’re all here. Three launches, four votes, and one archive with a very stubborn lock. I have time. The clock does not.

lines.speaker: mori
lines.text: I was up late again. I kept thinking about the people who never pick up a controller. Could we start with them?

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Oh! I have a poster for them. Is that weird? That’s weird. I’ll hold it.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: Hold it until after the vote, Slyvester. Your prototypes are make-believe. History stays under seal until the last page. Shall we begin?

lines.speaker: mori
lines.text: I visited three families who don’t own a console. Two shrugged. One asked, ‘Could my dad play too?’ I wrote that down.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Oh! Picture the commercial. Grandma bowls, Dad cheers, nobody asks about polygons. I can see the poster already. Retailers will ask what’s inside, though.

lines.speaker: grumble
lines.text: Cute poster, Slyvester. Now show me the bill for motion sensors and the six-word slogan you call a forecast.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Retailers don’t buy posters, Pawson. They buy feelings. Then they buy lunch.

lines.speaker: grumble
lines.text: I’m not buying either. Motion sensors aren’t free, and neither is my lunch.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: I can build a wand a kid can wave. Probably. The trick is making every wild swing count without hitting Pawson’s coffee.

lines.speaker: mori
lines.text: Who’s missing from the room? The parent who slips out when the console turns on. I keep thinking about her.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Okay, hear me out. Phones own the pocket and the spare minute. We need a living-room trick a glowing rectangle can’t do.

lines.speaker: grumble
lines.text: I like the poster, Slyvester. I don’t like the bill for two screens, two chargers, and one house already buried in cables. I brought a snack.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: A snack? Pawson, we’re launching a console, not a picnic.

lines.speaker: grumble
lines.text: You bring the console. I’ll bring the picnic. Mine has a budget.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Second screen in the controller? I can build that. Battery, latency, and price all want the same seat. Somebody’s getting shoved.

lines.speaker: mori
lines.text: One mother told me she loved playing together. Then she hid the second screen in a drawer. Did anyone ask her why?

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Premium is the language retailers speak. Skipping it is a gamble. I hate that I’m the one saying this.

lines.speaker: mori
lines.text: I asked people where they play. A train. A lunch break. A friend’s kitchen table. Nobody said the living room.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: I can build a dock, a battery, and detachable controls. Each one steals space from the other two, which is the fun part and the problem.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: One screen, two players, no setup. That’s six words, and I want it on every wall.

lines.speaker: grumble
lines.text: Slyvester’s poster is six words. The invoice has more pages. Show me what a customer gets for every extra gram.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: A gram of what? It’s a controller, not a sandwich.

lines.speaker: grumble
lines.text: Everything is a sandwich if you’re hungry enough. My point stands.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: I can make it lighter. I can make it cheaper. I can’t make it lighter, cheaper, and cool. Pick two.

lines.speaker: grumble
lines.text: Performance still sells. Ignoring it leaves money on the table, and I dislike leaving money anywhere.

lines.speaker: grumble
lines.text: A bigger box. More vents. A controller shaped like the last one. Enthusiasts will nod. My budget just fainted.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: Slyvester can sell the box. Pawson has to pay for the vents. A faster machine may win the shelf. Will it win a place at a family’s table?

lines.speaker: mori
lines.text: A room you understand in five minutes. I like that. The family has to feel play before anyone reads a manual.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: You’re inviting a new room to play. Hootley, keep an eye on the parent by the door. Can the first minute be fun before the manual?

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: One library in one hand. I love it. In 2005, the battery and the heat send you the bill before the fun starts.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: Damian, you’d carry the living room in one hand. Is the technology ready, or just early? I have time. The battery may not.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: The HD race is easy to explain. It’s also a race where the other runners know the track. I can sell it. I can’t make us faster.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: A premium machine speaks to players who already know the language. Slyvester can sell that. Can it give the rest of the house a reason to listen?

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: The second screen? I can build it. Making a whole family understand it at a glance is the hard part. Otherwise it’s an expensive coaster.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: The extra screen is memorable. Pawson will remember the chargers. Will a family remember why they needed it?

lines.speaker: grumble
lines.text: One portable library. Nice. Paying for premium expectations inside that shell is where the arithmetic starts growling.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: You chose freedom over the living room. Is that a new market, or a smaller one with better scenery? Damian, can it fit in a coat pocket?

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: A home-first machine can be sharp. It also asks the whole family to come to it. That’s a lot of walking.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: A home console can be the best seat in the house. What happens when the house empties and everyone wants to take the game along?

lines.speaker: mori
lines.text: Portability meets people where they are. It also leaves the shared room to other screens. I wonder which one gets lonely.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: One screen, always with you. A clean promise. Who gets left out when everyone plays alone, Hootley?

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Two places, one library. I can build that. The handoff has to feel invisible, or every dock becomes a chore.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: You’ve asked one device to live in two places. Will the experience travel as smoothly as the hardware? Damian, no spreadsheets.

lines.speaker: grumble
lines.text: Performance gives the enthusiasts a number to admire. It also puts every extra watt on someone’s bill.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: The enthusiasts will admire the number. Will a newcomer pick up the controller? Slyvester, make that the poster.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Two controllers from one. A spectator becomes a player before the commercial ends. That’s the demo. That’s the whole commercial.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: Two controllers from one is a generous invitation. Will the pieces still feel simple after a hundred family game nights? Pawson, bring snacks.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Motion can fill a room with laughter. It can also make the controller feel like a school fitness test.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: Motion can fill a room with laughter. Can it also keep the players who want a quiet evening? Pawson is already hiding.

lines.speaker: grumble
lines.text: Slyvester, that’s your poster again. Big numbers, family in the front room, no room for the family that doesn’t fit.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: One screen, two controllers, a friend joining before the commercial ends. Please use sturdy hinges. I know a beaver.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: A gesture-first home machine gets the whole room moving. Every game then answers to one unusual controller. Bring ice for the wrists.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Top performance in a handheld fights battery, heat, and your hand. You can win the spec sheet and lose the commute.

lines.speaker: mori
lines.text: A portable with two detachable controls invites a friend to join anywhere. It also asks everyone to keep track of more pieces. I’d lose one in a week.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: A gesture handheld turns one player into a tiny stage. Cute. The reason to carry it has to be louder than the wiggle.

lines.speaker: grumble
lines.text: You’ve got a dock, a screen, a battery, and a high-end chip all asking for the same space. Four mouths at one table. Slyvester, where’s the price story?

lines.speaker: mori
lines.text: The screen says two places. The controllers say bring a friend. Everything points the same way. Keep that one.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: The hybrid promise is already a mouthful. Making motion the centre adds spectacle and one more thing to explain before play.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: No peeking. Keep your reasoning warm. History can answer for itself.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: Still sealed. Four votes must be in before we compare our room with the company’s road.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: The archive has waited long enough. Let’s set your reasoning beside the record.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: You’ve picked a direction. Now make it a promise a family can repeat at breakfast.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: Two votes, one machine, one bet about how play fits into a life.

lines.speaker: shell
lines.text: The parts have to agree on one promise. Otherwise you’ve built a heavier box.
